name: Bristol Method
description: Air-bike cruise session: 4 minutes easy, then 6 rounds of 4 minutes at 80–85% max heart rate with 1 minute off the bike. Add one round when every round stays in that band, up to about 45–60 minutes. Curated from Jack Tyler's Bristol Method.
audience: Athletes who want low-impact aerobic work they can lengthen one round at a time, instead of sitting on the bike for a straight half hour
coachNotes: Rest is completely off the bike, not an easy pedal — heart rate should only partly come down. Keep every work round at 4 minutes and every rest at 1 minute. Start at 6 rounds. When you can hold 80–85% of max heart rate for all of them with a smooth cadence, add one round next session. Build toward 9–12 rounds (about 45–60 minutes). Do not make the rounds harder to progress. Repeat on days you are not already cooked. A published example held about 60 rpm to sit in that heart-rate band; use cadence to stay in the band, not as the goal.

days.name: Bristol Method
days.sessionPad: Warm-up: 4 min easy, about 57 rpm, then step off for 1 min. Work: 6 × 4 min at 80–85% max heart rate, 1 min completely off the bike. Smooth cadence — about 60 rpm is a common place to start. Add one round next time every round stays in the band. Stop around 9–12 rounds (45–60 min).

exercises.notes: Easy spin, about 57 rpm. Then stay off the bike for the full minute before the first work round.

80–85% max heart rate. Nudge cadence (about 60 rpm is a common start) so heart rate stays in the band. Step off the bike for the whole minute. Add one round when all 6 stay in the band; stop the build at 9–12 rounds.
